injuries.short: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injuries.long: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

injuries.short: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
injuries.long: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

injuries.short: Flemings (back) practiced Tuesday, per Lauren L. Williams of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution.
injuries.long: The rookie first-rounder missed Sunday's win in Milwaukee with a back injury, but he's making progress toward his return. Flemings can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable tag for Wednesday's game in Oklahoma City.

injuries.short: Landale (hip) is out for Sunday's game against Bucks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injuries.long: Landale missed four games earlier this month with a left hip issue, and he'll sit out Sunday due to right hip inflammation. Look for Zuby Ejiofor to see more minutes behind starter Onyeke Okongwu with Landale out of commission Sunday.

injuries.short: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injuries.long: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

injuries.short: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
injuries.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

injuries.short: Queta (rest) won't play in Monday's game against the Magic, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
injuries.long: The big man is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set Monday, but he should be good to go for Wednesday's showdown in Denver. Mitchell Robinson is the most likely choice to replace Queta in the starting lineup, while Luka Garza should see a sizable chunk of the center minutes.

injuries.short: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
injuries.long: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

injuries.short: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injuries.long: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

injuries.short: Williams (finger) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
injuries.long: After suffering a dislocated right pinky finger in Monday's loss to the Cavaliers, Williams is expected to play Wednesday. The 25-year-old forward is averaging 7.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 steals across 22.7 minutes per contest in six regular-season appearances.

injuries.short: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
injuries.long: Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

injuries.short: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

injuries.short: Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Chicago.
injuries.long: Tyson was downgraded to doubtful earlier in the day, and the team has since reported that he'll be held out of Monday's action due to right ankle injury management. Look for Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor and Tristan Enaruna to see more run in Tyson's absence.

injuries.short: Watson left Monday's 126-115 win over Chicago due to a head injury and did not return.
injuries.long: As expected, Watson missed the remainder of Cleveland's victory after taking a nasty fall on a drive to the basket with a little more than five minutes left in the game. He recorded 14 points (5-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and one blocks across 22 minutes. We'll know more once the Cavs provide an update on Watson's status moving forward.

injuries.short: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
injuries.long: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

injuries.short: Merrill (elbow) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bulls.
injuries.long: Merrill is set to miss his sixth consecutive game due to a right elbow injury. With the majority of the Cavs' starting lineup expected to return versus Chicago, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas should continue to see the majority of Merrill's vacated minutes in the backcourt.

injuries.short: Tomlin is set to miss several weeks with a lower back stress reaction, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
injuries.long: This is a tough blow for the forward and there's no guarantee he's cleared right away when he's re-evaluated in three-to-four weeks. Tomlin wasn't projected to crack the rotation ahead of Opening Night and was penciled in to be an emergency depth option.

injuries.short: Christie (ankle) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injuries.long: Christie sat out Dallas' last two games but is trending in the right direction before Wednesday's meeting with the Warriors. He's averaged just 9.5 minutes per game in his last four appearances, but the swingman's return would still leave fewer minutes available for Caleb Martin and Zaccharie Risacher.

injuries.short: Aldama (ankle) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injuries.long: Aldama missed Sunday's loss to Boston with a left ankle sprain but is trending in the right direction ahead of Wednesday's game against Golden State. His return would leave fewer minutes available for guys like Morez Johnson and Caleb Martin.

injuries.short: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
injuries.long: Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland. He will, however, sit out the second leg of the back-to-back for Dallas, which will likely send Cooper Flagg's usage to the moon. Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton Jr. should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

injuries.short: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game in Minnesota.
injuries.long: Lively is still working his way back from foot surgery. He's reportedly trending favorably, though he should continue to be classified as week-to-week, at least until the team provides an update. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with Morez Johnson (shin), Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse all in line to spend time at the five when needed.

injuries.short: Biberovic (heel) is out for Thursday's game against Minnesota.
injuries.long: Biberovic remains plagued by right heel bursitis. The rookie forward carries no timetable for his season debut.

injuries.short: De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Minnesota.
injuries.long: De Larrea hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a right knee sprain, but he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Still, he can be considered week-to-week until Dallas provides an update on his progress.

injuries.short: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
injuries.long: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

injuries.short: Joe (hip) is out for Tuesday's game against the Spurs.
injuries.long: Joe has been sidelined since late October with a bruised hip. He has a short turnaround ahead of Wednesday's matchup in New Orleans for a possible return.

injuries.short: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
injuries.long: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

injuries.short: Prince (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Spurs.
injuries.long: Prince made just his third appearance of the season during Saturday's 137-117 loss to Miami, finishing with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one assists in eight minutes. However, he'll now miss his 10th overall outing as he deals with soreness in his right knee. Prince's absence shouldn't have an impact on the rotation, and his next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus New Orleans.

injuries.short: Holland is out for Tuesday's game against San Antonio due to a left knee contusion.
injuries.long: It's not clear as to when Holland picked up the injury, but it's significant enough to shut him down for at least one game. His next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday in New Orleans.

injuries.short: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

injuries.short: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

injuries.short: Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com.
injuries.long: Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backourt.

injuries.short: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injuries.long: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injuries.short: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injuries.short: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

injuries.short: Capela (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Indiana.
injuries.long: Capela is still recovering from a right ankle sprain and will remain on the inactive list for a ninth straight game. The veteran center's next opportunity to play will come Friday at Denver.

injuries.short: Thompson (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
injuries.long: Thompson is looking to end a one-game absence Wednesday due to a knee issue. Reed Sheppard has a chance to play a considerable role off the bench if Thompson sits out.

injuries.short: Phillips (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
injuries.long: Phillips will shake off his questionable tag for Wednesday's regular-season opener. However, the two-way player isn't likely to be part of the Rockets' rotation.

injuries.short: Head coach Rick Carlisle said Tuesday that Haliburton (hamstring) is "getting there," but there's still no definitive timetable for his return to game action, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
injuries.long: Carlisle wouldn't rule out a return in November, though he added that there's "nothing happening in the near-term." The star point guard hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and until he's cleared to return, Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties while Quenton Jackson sees increased burn.

injuries.short: Nembhard (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.long: Nembhard will miss his third contest of the season due to left hip soreness. T.J. McConnell should slide into the first unit while Quenton Jackson gets a boost in minutes off the bench.

injuries.short: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
injuries.long: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

injuries.short: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injuries.short: Niederhauser (foot) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
injuries.long: Niederhauser has yet to make his season debut for the Clippers while recovering from Lisfranc surgery on his right foot. He should still be considered week-to-week until stated otherwise.

injuries.short: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Friday's game against the Thunder, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injuries.long: Ingram is ramping up his activity as he nears his season debut for the Clippers, but he's not yet cleared for game action amid his Achilles rehab. Until the star forward is ready to suit up, Kris Dunn, Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones should all hang onto starting roles.

injuries.short: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injuries.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

injuries.short: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injuries.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injuries.short: Reaves (heel) is out for Tuesday's game against the Hornets, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.long: Reaves will miss a second consecutive matchup while tending to a bruised left heel. Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams should continue to see more minutes in Reaves' absence. His next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday against Utah.

injuries.short: Walker (leg) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Hornets.
injuries.long: Kessler will miss his first game of the season due to right lower leg soreness. Expect Sandro Mamukelashvili, Jarred Vanderbilt and Kevon Looney to share the load with Kessler sidelined.

injuries.short: Stewart is out for Monday's game against the Wizards due to an illness.
injuries.long: The big man can be considered day-to-day ahead of Wednesday's meeting in Cleveland. A big workload could be in store for Zach Edey (ankle) if he's able to play for the Grizzlies on Monday.

injuries.short: Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
injuries.long: Jerome will miss a second straight matchup while nursing right hip soreness. Cam Spencer could receive another chance to start at point guard in Jerome's absence. The Virginia product's next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday in Cleveland.

injuries.short: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
injuries.long: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injuries.short: Jackson will undergo surgery to repair the broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot and is set to miss significant time.
injuries.long: The Grizzlies will release a timeline for Jackson's return to basketball activities after he undergoes surgery, though he's facing a lengthy absence. With the 22-year-old forward on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant are candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.short: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injuries.short: Jovic (illness) is out for Monday's game against Houston.
injuries.long: Jovic was added to the injury report as questionable due to an illness earlier in the day Monday, and the club has since determined that he won't be able to give it a go. Klay Thompson and Bobby Portis could pick up a few additional minutes in Jovic's absence, though the impact to Miami's rotation should be minimal.

injuries.short: Coach Erik Spoelstra stated after Monday's 128-110 win over Houston that the team held Adebayo (hip) out of the second half in an effort to be proactive, and the injury isn't expected to be a long-term issue, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
injuries.long: This is positive news for the star center, who didn't come out of the locker room to start the second half of Monday's clash. Miami will presumably re-evaluate Adebayo over the next few days to determine whether he'll be able to suit up for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee.

injuries.short: Rollins (illness) is out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
injuries.long: Rollins will miss his first game of the season due to an illness. Gary Trent, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis are candidates for increased roles with Rollins sidelined.

injuries.short: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
injuries.long: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

injuries.short: Pullin (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
injuries.long: Pullin will miss Tuesday's contest with a right quadriceps contusion, though his absence shouldn't affect the rotation. His next chance to play will come Thursday against New York.

injuries.short: Kuminga (shoulder) is out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
injuries.long: Kuminga sustained a bruised shoulder during Monday's meeting with the Trail Blazers, and he's sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Terrence Shannon appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Kuminga in the starting lineup, while Trey Lyles and Bones Hyland will both have a chance to claim a larger role.

injuries.short: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
injuries.long: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

injuries.short: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injuries.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injuries.short: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injuries.short: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injuries.long: Mathurin will miss a third straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the short-handed Pelicans moving forward.

injuries.short: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injuries.long: McGowens will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. It's unclear how far along he is in his recovery.

injuries.short: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injuries.long: Watford will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a definitive return timeline.

injuries.short: Murphy (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
injuries.long: The star forward is missing a sixth consecutive contest with bilateral knee tendinopathy. Saddiq Bey should remain rostered in all fantasy leagues while Murphy is on the shelf.

injuries.short: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injuries.long: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injuries.short: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Kings.
injuries.long: Williams will miss a sixth straight contest due to lower-back spasms and is still without a timetable to return. Isaiah Hartenstein, Kenrich Williams and rookie Aday Mara will continue holding down the frontcourt for as long as Williams is sidelined.

injuries.short: Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long: Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

injuries.short: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injuries.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injuries.short: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injuries.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injuries.short: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.long: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injuries.short: Nelson (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
injuries.long: Nelson underwent surgery to repair his fractured left ankle this offseason and has yet to make his NBA debut. He remains without a firm timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.short: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
injuries.long: Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

injuries.short: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injuries.long: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

injuries.short: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injuries.short: Brown (hamstring/head) will undergo further evaluation Tuesday and could receive an MRI, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Brown turned in a stellar performance with 31 points and 13 rebounds in Monday's win over Brooklyn, but he also dealt with left hamstring tightness and an apparent head issue that contributed to him sitting out the final 1:44 of regulation. The fact that the 30-year-old played through the ailments down the stretch could be an encouraging sign, though he'll undergo further evaluation Tuesday and an MRI is a possibility. Philadelphia's next game is Wednesday at Orlando, and if Brown is sidelined, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons could see an uptick in playing time.

injuries.short: James (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nets.
injuries.long: As expected, James won't play in the second half of Philly's back-to-back set after finishing Sunday's 131-124 victory over Indiana with 15 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and one block across 33 minutes. The veteran superstar has yet to play in both halves of a back-to-back set this season, and that trend is unlikely to change. Dean Wade and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased roles in James' absence.

injuries.short: Barlow (back) will be re-evaluated later in the week and is thought to be nearing his 2026-27 season debut, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long: Barlow has yet to take the court this season due to a back injury, but he's trending in the right direction. He was spotted participating in shootaround Thursday, and if all goes well during his re-evaluation, the team could have additional news on when he'll make his season debut.

injuries.short: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
injuries.long: The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

injuries.short: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injuries.short: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

injuries.short: Avdija (foot) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Timberwolves.
injuries.long: After playing 30 minutes during Monday's loss to Minnesota, the star point forward is in danger of missing the second half of this back-to-back set. Damian Lillard would do the heavy lifting offensively if Avdija sits out Tuesday, while either Jrue Holiday or Scoot Henderson would likely enter the starting lineup.

injuries.short: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game at Minnesota.
injuries.long: Youngblood will miss a fourth consecutive contest with what the team is now calling a right heel bone bruise. His next opportunity to play will come Thursday at Milwaukee.

injuries.short: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.long: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

injuries.short: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
injuries.long: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

injuries.short: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

injuries.short: LaVine is out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City due to illness, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
injuries.long: LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.

injuries.short: Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
injuries.long: Hunter was added to the injury report close to tipoff, and he's since been downgraded to out. The Kings will be forced to play shorthanded Sunday, as Precious Achiuwa (ankle) and Zach LaVine (illness) are also unavailable. The absence of three starters should open up minutes for Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk.

injuries.short: Achiuwa (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
injuries.long: Achiuwa is battling with ankle soreness and will miss a second straight game while on the mend. Keegan Murray drew the start in Achiuwa's absence Friday and is a good candidate to do so again Sunday evening.

injuries.short: Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
injuries.long: Raynaud will miss his 13th consecutive game to start 2026-27 after injuring his knee during the preseason. It sounds like the Frenchman is getting closer to making his season debut, with his next chance to do so coming Wednesday versus Phoenix.

injuries.short: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injuries.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injuries.short: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injuries.long: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

injuries.short: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injuries.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injuries.short: Barnes (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injuries.long: Barnes was a late addition to the injury report and could sit out the front end of this back-to-back set. If the star forward is unable to suit up, Jakob Poeltl, Kyle Anderson and Allen Graves would all be candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.short: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injuries.long: Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

injuries.short: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injuries.long: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

injuries.short: Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Leonard (knee) is doing individual on-court work and is progressing well, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
injuries.long: The Raptors are expected to provide another update on Leonard's status in about one week, though it's encouraging to see how he's progressed thus far. Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased playing time for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

injuries.short: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long: Hayes will miss a second consecutive game due to a left knee strain, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday in the second half of the Jazz's back-to-back set. Mo Bamba is likely to remain in the starting lineup after faring well in his first start Sunday. On the year, Hayes is averaging 8.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 blocks across 12 appearances (10 starts).

injuries.short: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

injuries.short: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
injuries.long: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

injuries.short: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

injuries.short: Okpara (illness) is available for Friday's game against Toronto.
injuries.long: Okpara will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up Friday. However, the two-way player isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

injuries.short: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis.
injuries.long: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

injuries.short: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
injuries.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

injuries.short: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injuries.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injuries.short: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
injuries.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
